slides.header: Your team's notch, now an AI command center.
slides.subtitle: SparkV Team: a 30-day pilot for up to 5 seats
body: Dictation, meetings, search and screen help, on device
Private by default. Deploys with your MDM.
sparkv.si
slides.notes: SparkV lives in the MacBook notch. Hover it and a drawer opens with media, a file tray, your day and a hub of more than 20 agents. Today we are asking for one thing: a 30-day pilot with up to five people on your team. We measure the time it saves against a baseline you set, and you decide on day 30.

slides.subtitle: Talking about work and looking for things crowd out the work itself
body: 57% | of Microsoft 365 users' time goes to communicating; 43% to creating | Microsoft Work Trend Index 2023
19% | of interaction workers' time goes to searching for and gathering information | McKinsey Global Institute, 2012
68% | say they lack enough uninterrupted focus time | Microsoft Work Trend Index 2023
3x | faster text entry by speech than a phone keyboard (English) | Stanford, Baidu, UW study, 2016
[TBD: your team's own baseline, measured in pilot week 1]
slides.notes: Four public numbers frame the problem. Caveats to say out loud: the 3x figure compares speech with a phone keyboard, not a desktop keyboard, so the ROI model on slide 9 uses a much smaller gain. The McKinsey figure is from 2012. The pilot replaces all of these with your own baseline.

kpis.label: of time spent searching for and gathering information

slides.subtitle: Hover the notch and the drawer opens. Move away and it closes.
body: Write: dictation, reply drafts, prompt refiner
Meet: recording, notes, live answers, translation
Find: Spaces and Universal Search (⌥Space)
See: ask about any screen, copy text from any pixel
Ship: UI Audit, Browser Flows, Flow Canvas
slides.notes: This is the Agents hub: 22 tiles in an 8 by 3 grid, every one wired in the current build. A tile opens its page, runs at once, or shows a menu. Hover a tile to see its shortcut. Everything in this deck is reachable from here or from a hotkey.

slides.header: Write at the speed of speech
slides.subtitle: Hold fn, talk, release. Clean text lands where the cursor is.
body: Dictate into any text field: filler words removed, lists formatted
⌃⌥R drafts a reply in your tone; you review and press Send
⌘⇧V opens the clipboard stack at the cursor
Clipboard history stays off until the user turns it on
slides.notes: Dictation types into any app. Reply Drafter reads the thread and writes into the message box; it never sends. Clipboard history is off by default and skips passwords and private copies. Status: dictation and Reply Drafter are marked 'needs a live check' in the feature guide because they need the microphone, the fn key and other apps; the pilot is that check.

slides.header: Meeting notes, no bot in the call
slides.subtitle: One click records the mic and the call audio. Transcription runs on the Mac.
body: Minutes, decisions and your tasks with due days
Suggested answers when someone asks you a question
Live captions translate other speakers, on device
Filed to the right client Space automatically
slides.notes: No bot joins the call, so there is nothing for the other side to admit. Your policy on telling participants about recording still applies: [TBD: customer's call-recording notice policy]. Live Translation uses Apple Translation on device after a one-time language download. Status: needs a live check (audio capture); notes and answers render from saved meetings.

slides.header: Every client in its own Space
slides.subtitle: Find anything you saw, heard or copied. Ask about anything on screen.
body: Spaces file meetings, notes, mail, pages and screenshots per client
⌥Space searches Spaces, meetings, dictations, clipboard and Tray
Ask mode answers from your own items, with citations
Hold ⌃⌥ and ask about any app; SparkV points at the spot
slides.notes: Built for agencies with several clients. Be exact about sharing: a Space can be exported and shared as a .sparkvspace file package; there is no live sync between teammates today. The screen assistant points and explains; it does not click or type. Without a Groq key it reads screen text on device. Status: Spaces and Universal Search verified headless (21 results for 'launch' on sample data); the screen assistant needs a live check.

slides.header: QA client sites before they ship
slides.subtitle: UI Audit walks your site like a tester, then writes the fix prompt
body: Crawls pages, fills forms on test hosts, checks 1440 px and 390 px
Accessibility (axe-core), Tab order, console errors, failed requests
Findings by severity, with screenshot and steps to reproduce
P copies a fix prompt for Claude Code, Cursor or Copilot
Verified run on our test site: 6 pages, 69 findings, 3 critical, 15 high
slides.notes: This is the one feature verified end to end: SparkV's own controller audited the bundled planted-issue test site on 127.0.0.1 (6 pages, 69 findings: 3 critical, 15 high), Apple Intelligence wrote the summary on device, and P produced a 51,666-character fix prompt covering 60 issues. The runner self-test passed 48/48. It submits forms only on local or test hosts unless allowed and never clicks Delete or Log out unless allowed. Needs Node 20+ and Playwright's Chromium. Use only on sites you own or may test.

slides.header: About 2.5 hours back per person, per week
slides.subtitle: A model to test in the pilot, not a measured result
body: 150 min | modeled time saved per person per week | Model (assumptions below)
$96 | Team list price per seat per year | SparkV pricing
~3 min | saved per week pays for a seat at $40/hour | Example rate, [TBD: your loaded rate]
Assumptions are conservative and replaced by measured values in the pilot
slides.notes: Walk through the assumptions table, not the total. Dictation uses a 1.5x speed-up, half of the published 3x, because that study used a phone keyboard. Break-even formula: minutes per week = 96 / (46 working weeks x hourly rate) x 60. At $40 an hour that is about 3.1 minutes a week. The hourly rate is the buyer's number; $40 is only an example.

slides.subtitle: AI runs on the Mac. Nothing leaves unless someone turns it on.

columns.title: Stays on the Mac
bullets: AI: Apple Intelligence, Vision, Speech, Translation
Keys stored in the macOS Keychain

columns.title: Leaves only by choice
bullets: Groq: opt-in per feature, with your own key
Sends the screenshot under the pointer and the question, only while asking
License check: key, anonymous device ID, app version to Lemon Squeezy

body: Clipboard history off by default; passwords skipped
No meeting bot
Recorded browser passwords never saved
Face Unlock not in the sold build
slides.notes: This slide is the security reviewer's summary. Default: on-device Apple Intelligence; AI cost to us is $0, so there is no reason to route data to a server. Groq is optional, per feature, and uses the customer's own key; nothing uses it unless turned on. Licensing talks to Lemon Squeezy, the merchant of record. Face Unlock is excluded from the sold build because its face model is licensed for non-commercial use only. Gap to disclose: there is no admin-enforced switch to block Groq org-wide yet [TBD: managed preference to disable Groq].

body: Status: signing, notarization, licensing and the .pkg are on the 1.0 checklist. The pilot runs on the notarized 1.0 build. [TBD: 1.0 date]
Requires Apple silicon and macOS 15+. Node 20+ only for UI Audit and Browser Flows.
slides.notes: Be candid: today's build is signed with a local identity. Developer ID signing, notarization, licensing and the MDM package are tasks in the 30-day launch plan, and the pilot starts on that build. On permissions: an MDM privacy profile (PPPC) can pre-approve Accessibility; Screen Recording can at most be made approvable by standard users; camera and microphone always need the user's own approval. Verify against Apple's PPPC payload documentation for the customer's macOS version. With one stable Developer ID, grants survive updates.

slides.subtitle: One invoice, simple seats, and a person who answers

rows.label: Seats
rows.text: 1 seat = 1 person on 2 Macs. Minimum 3 seats. Move a Mac by deactivating it in the gear menu.

rows.label: Admin
rows.text: Assign and revoke seats in the Lemon Squeezy customer portal. One invoice, PO or bank transfer.

rows.label: Resilience
rows.text: Checks the license every 7 days, 14 days offline grace. Never locks: falls back to Free and keeps data.

rows.label: Support
rows.text: Priority email, 1 business day. Signed automatic updates. 30-day refund.

slides.notes: Disclose what does not exist: no SSO or SCIM, no central policy console beyond the seat portal, and shared Spaces are file packages without live sync. Seat management may run on Keygen instead of Lemon Squeezy if needed. Updates ship through Sparkle with EdDSA-signed feeds. Support contact: [TBD: support email].

slides.subtitle: Overlapping tools, per seat, year one, list prices

Monthly prices are annualized x12 for year one. NotchNook and Alcove are left out of the stack bar because SparkV replaces them outright and they are one-time.
